analysis.summary: This PR introduces a structure mismatch in the discount data consumption on the frontend and an invalid property access on an array in the BFF, which will prevent discounts from being displayed.

bugs.title: Incorrect nesting of discount data in LineCard
bugs.description: The code casts 'minBadgePrice' (type PriceWithPromotion) directly to PromotionPriceEntry. However, according to the BFF interfaces, the discount details (discountedFormattedValue, totalDiscountPercentage) are nested inside minBadgePrice.promotionPrice.discount or netDiscount.
bugs.risk: The DiscountPricing component will receive an object with an incorrect structure (PriceWithPromotion instead of PromotionPriceEntry). As a result, all discount-related fields (price, badge, percentages) will be undefined at runtime, causing the discount UI to fail to render correctly on line cards.

bugs.title: Invalid property access on array in product-model BFF
bugs.description: The 'getProducts' function returns the result of Promise.all, which is an array of wrapped response objects. The handler tries to access 'products.lineCategories' directly on this array, which will be undefined.
bugs.risk: The 'lineCategories' data, which contains the critical 'minBadgePrice' information for the customizer lines, will be missing (undefined) from the BFF response. This breaks the discount display logic for the entire 'LineCard' overview feature.

notBugs.reason: The useEffect added in products-context.tsx for syncing selectedVehicle is gated by a check (selectedVehicle.pn18 !== state.product.code), preventing an infinite loop despite updating the dependent state via setProduct.

While the cast to PromotionPriceEntry is risky (and part of a functional bug), the use of type assertions like 'as PromotionPriceEntry' is noted as a developer's explicit declaration and is only reported here because it directly causes a demonstrated structural mismatch.
